lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

measurements.source: proposal.md geometry figures plus reading of preview-letter.png. No layout.json exists. geometry.json was not re-parsed because the protocol allows only 6 tool calls.
measurements.left_edges: Cocktails x 60; lower tier x 60 / 354 / 615 with equal 84 px gutters: pass within each tier. The upper tier (one 380 px measure, navy column at 452, headhouse at 496, bins at 594) shares no column line with lower-tier columns 2 and 3 (354, 615), so the page has two unrelated grids.
measurements.headers: H2s share y 672 and H3s share y 704 across the lower tier. There is one style per level (DM Sans 600 caps #8F4F10; Fraunces italic subheads): pass
measurements.item_spacing: First items at 736. Second groups at 860 (Brandy, Sparkling) and 918 (Cider). Gaps are constant within each column.
measurements.price_eye_travel: Prices are inline 0.75 em (about 14 px) after the name, about 4% of the 380 px cocktail measure and under 10% of the 142-210 px lower columns. No row is over 40%: pass
measurements.price_format: Integers everywhere, no $, tabular figures, muted Fraunces at name size: consistent
measurements.accent_area_pct_reading_layer: 0.10 in cocktails, 0.11 in the lower tier
measurements.bleed: 12 css px = 3.2 mm, which passes the 3 mm minimum by 0.2 mm
measurements.dead_space: About 58 px (15 mm) is dead under Spirits and Wine, and about 250 px of paper in the display preview sits under the short columns at the bottom. The navy sliver between the cocktail panel edge (452) and the headhouse (496) is 44 px and reads as an accidental gutter.

remove: The navy ink mottling. At viewing size it reads as a speckled digital-noise or carpet texture, which is on J5's own avoid-list, not as flat screen-print ink. A clean flat navy with only the amber misregistration trap line would carry the print idea more honestly.
top_problem: The fusion idea (a papel-picado horizon under an Iowa grain elevator) is real, but the art does not deliver it. The paper elevator reads as an abstract tower block plus a colonnade: the navy seams with flared tops look like column capitals or goblet stems, the domes do not read, and the leg housing reads as a chimney. The zig-zag and rombo band reads as generic Mexican rickrack trim, not cut tissue with light through it. Next to ref-02 panels 1-2 it is a tidy two-tier list with a borrowed CANTINA wordmark (the same tracked Didone-style caps as ref-02) and trim, well short of an unforgettable gesture. The boldest missing idea is a single monumental elevator silhouette that is itself cut like papel picado: pierced rombos and picos punched through the bins so the amber dusk shows through the paper. Mexico and Iowa would then fuse in one object, not stack as a building and a border.
fixes: Fuse the two motifs into one object. Pierce the papel-picado grammar (picos along the bin crowns, rombos through the bin walls) into the elevator itself, let the amber show through, and cut the separate full-width amber band down to a thin horizon line. This addresses criteria 15, 16 and 7.

Redraw the bins so they read as cylinders at thumbnail: tonal half-round shading in a second paper value, or a curved crown silhouette against navy, instead of navy Y-shaped seams. Remove the chimney-like leg housing, or make it clearly narrower and offset so it reads as the elevator leg.

Lock one page grid across both tiers. Put lower-tier columns 2 and 3 on lines the art already defines (for example Beer at the navy column edge at 452 and Wine at the bin start at 594), so the elevator and the list share structure instead of sitting on two unrelated grids.

Remove the dead space at the bottom. Either reflow to two lower columns of equal height (Spirits+Wine | Beer & Cider), or raise the horizon band so all columns end within 1 baseline of the bottom margin. The 58 px spread and the empty floor under Spirits and Wine read as unfinished.

Make the wordmark ownable. The tracked high-contrast CANTINA caps are lifted almost verbatim from ref-02 panels 1-2. Set it so it interacts with the art (for example standing on the gallery line or partly cut by the headhouse) and so it cannot be swapped onto any cantina.

lens: items and prices vs draft_doc.json; ingredient names and description completeness (public_components); flow
top_problem: The spirits lines, the main change this round, read as database classes rather than guest language. 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour' take NOM-006 taxonomy paths word for word. The middot makes 'pour' look like an ingredient. 'agave spirit' is vaguer than the item name, which already says Tequila. 'Grape brandy from Cognac' is close to a tautology. All three nodes are proposal_status=proposed, so the facts are not approved. These are the weakest descriptions on a cantina menu whose lead category is agave.
problems: Prices: all 14 items match the draft exactly (15/15/14/16, 7/8/7/8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). Nothing is invented, dropped or changed. Criterion 9 = 100.

Items: all 14 draft items are present, and so is Dry Cider from the draft's separate Cider section (items listed at section level, with no subs). The designer disclosed three structural edits to the draft: Cider is folded into a 'Beer & Cider' heading, Margarita now leads Classics ahead of Manhattan, and Spirits moves up from fourth to fifth... correction: Spirits moves up from fourth place in the draft to lead the lower tier. None is an invention, but the section names no longer match the draft's venue_heading values ('Beer', 'Cider').

Manhattan: aromatic bitters is correctly hidden (public_components aromatic-bitters=false). The line now reads as a 2-ingredient-plus-garnish build, which is thin for the house's signature stirred drink. That is correct behaviour, just a thin result.

Garnishes (Margarita lime wheel, Daiquiri lime coin, Old Fashioned orange peel) are not in draft_doc.json. The proposal sources them to recipe_versions (rv f06abb74, 14d45e57, 7095fd3d). That is acceptable as an input, but the Accuracy reviewer has to confirm the rows. 'Lime coin' is bartender jargon that guests may not know.

The Brown Butter Old Fashioned has public_visibility.house_recipe=false. Printing both house preps (brown butter-washed bourbon and demerara syrup) is borderline. The draft's own desc names them too, so this is not a gate fail, but the Coordinator should confirm what house_recipe=false is meant to hide.

Description line breaks drop the separator, so 'Tequila blanco · fresh lime juice / orange liqueur…' and 'Brown butter-washed bourbon / demerara syrup…' read as two separate lists instead of one list that wraps.
Voice: only the Margarita carries a tasting note ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). One item in fourteen with a flavour line reads as inconsistent, not deliberate.
Dry-Hopped IPA → 'Hop-forward draft IPA' repeats the name. Brief §5 keeps it, but it still adds nothing for the guest.

Data gap (not the designer's fault, already with Rob): beer and cider have no ABV, wine has no region or producer (Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé say only 'Dry red/white/sparkling'), and spirits have no brand, age statement or pour size. The proposal flags this correctly, but criterion 8 cannot reach professional level until the data arrives.

Flow: the entry point is clear (wordmark → Cocktails → amber band → three columns), and agave leading the lower tier suits a cantina. Categories are not treated equally, though. Cocktails get a 380 px measure over half the page, while Wine is pushed into a 142 px far-right column that ends early. The Beer & Cider column hangs 58 px below its neighbours, and the bottom of the page is empty, so the lower tier reads as an afterthought.

Price format is consistent: no $, whole numbers, tabular figures, set 0.75 em after the name, with short eye travel and no association risk. It works but is ordinary. Glass pour sizes and bottle prices are not labelled; the draft has no labels, so nothing is wrong.
fixes: Rewrite the three spirits lines in guest language from the approved facts only, without the 'pour' token or the '-class' wording: for example 'Unaged blanco tequila' / 'Añejo tequila, barrel-aged' / 'VSOP Cognac, grape brandy'. Flag them missing_ingredients until the taxonomy nodes are approved and Rob supplies brand and pour size.
Keep the middot, or use a comma, at every description line break so each wrapped list reads as one build, not two.
Either drop the Margarita's lone tasting note or ask Rob for draft-sourced tasting notes for every cocktail, so the voice is consistent across the section.
Give the lower-tier categories equal weight: widen the Wine column, or rebalance the columns so Wine is not the narrowest and last, and close the 58 px spread and the empty space at the page bottom.

Get Coordinator sign-off on the three structural edits (Beer & Cider merge, Margarita before Manhattan, Spirits promoted), and confirm with the Accuracy reviewer that the rv garnish rows exist and that printing the house preps on the Old Fashioned (house_recipe=false) is allowed.

lens: Ingredient, garnish and label tracing (build/draft_doc.json, phg.menu_items / phg.recipe_versions gateway log 228, public.beverage_categories gateway log 229) plus how descriptions and prices sit together in explore-J5/preview-letter.png
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but the spirits lines are raw taxonomy text: 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour' come from beverage_categories nodes 04d72e1f (name 'Blanco / plata', authority_note 'NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §5, clase'), 9f4dae69 ('Añejo'), parent 6267d9c9 ('Agave & desert spirits') and c1ad100b/a88f6e79/bec5063c (Grape brandy > Cognac > VSOP), and all of those nodes are proposal_status='proposed'. That wording is the scorecard's automatic-fail case for criterion 12 ('read like database classes'). It also misleads a US guest: on a US label, 'agave spirit' is the TTB class for spirits that are not tequila, so on a cantina menu it undersells the house's own tequilas. Add the name-echo lines ('Hop-forward draft IPA' for Dry-Hopped IPA 8fb136cd, 'Toasty amber lager' for Amber Lager 70657e1e, 'Dry sparkling cider' for Dry Cider 65c39a14, 'Dry red wine' / 'Dry white wine' for Malbec f6f9d57e / Pinot Grigio 5ba7511f) and the lower tier has no guest voice at all. Verified sources: the garnishes lime wheel, cocktail cherry, lime coin and orange peel match recipe_versions f06abb74, 9fb77eaa, 14d45e57 and 7095fd3d. The components (tequila blanco, fresh lime juice, orange liqueur, agave syrup, rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, white rum, demerara syrup, brown butter-washed bourbon, aromatic bitters) match draft_doc components. The Manhattan bitters are correctly hidden (public_components aromatic-bitters=false). 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is sentence 2 of menu_items 14555870.menu_description. Dry Cider 8 is sourced from menu_items 65c39a14 (the draft_doc Cider section is empty). All 14 prices match menu_items.menu_price, and each sits inline 0.75em after its own name, so there is no association risk. No brand, ABV, region, age statement or glassware is printed beyond the sources (known gap, awaiting Rob). The sub-line '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' states no item fact. Note: menu_items 57617f46 'Junmai Ginjo' (12) is in the project but absent from the draft doc and the menu; Content should confirm the exclusion is intended.
fixes: Rewrite the three spirits lines in guest language from the same rows, with no '-class' or 'agave spirit' taxonomy words. For example: 'Unaged tequila, served neat' for Blanco (node 04d72e1f; 'unaged' also needs a source row, so confirm it or drop it), 'Aged tequila, served neat' for Añejo (node 9f4dae69), 'VSOP Cognac, served neat' for Cognac VSOP (bec5063c, draft desc 'VSOP Cognac pour.'). Flag pour size as missing rather than printing a bare 'pour'.

Replace the name-echo beer, cider and wine descriptions once Rob supplies style, region and producer. Until then, flag them as missing_ingredients in the proposal rather than printing 'Dry red wine' under Malbec and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' under Dry-Hopped IPA, because as printed they add nothing and fail criterion 12.

Make the voice consistent: either give every cocktail a one-line sourced tasting note like the Margarita's (only if the draft supplies it; otherwise ask), or move the Margarita note into the same line style. As set, one italic note on one of four cocktails reads as an accident, not a system.

Venue fit for a Mexican cantina in Iowa City: set the section and sub heads in correct Spanish with the English kept as the reading aid (e.g. 'Cócteles', 'Clásicos', 'De la Casa', 'Cervezas y Sidra', 'Vinos', 'Destilados' / 'Agave'). Tell Rob that the draft list (Manhattan, House Daiquiri, Czech Pilsner, Malbec, Cognac, no mezcal and no Mexican beer) could belong to any bar, and that $14-16 cocktails sit high for a college-town market.

Label the pours and serves: Brut Rosé 13 under 'Sparkling' has no glass/bottle label (the draft price label is empty, so ask Rob and flag it rather than guess), and the spirits need a pour size. Rebalance the Old Fashioned break ('Brown butter-washed bourbon' alone, then a long second line) so the two lines are closer in length: note for the designer.
